design.task: 10-option multiple choice; exactly 1 correct option per task; 20 tasks; generateFn candidates are correct independently with probability 0.2
design.scoring: scoreFn returns 1 for the correct option and 0 otherwise; final correctness is graded externally by parsing the last option letter

budget.enforcement: the wrapper returns [] and records an overflow after either cap; all strategies are checked for overflow
budget.note: generateCalls counts generateFn invocations; candidates counts returned answers. best_of_n makes 20 calls of n=1; MCTS makes 10 calls of n=2; guided beam makes 1 call of n=20.

design.commonRandomNumbers: each task seeds the same candidate stream for every arm; arms differ only in how many candidates they request and how they select

taskTypes.mcts_math: math (control; candidate text matches "the answer is")

rule: add-opt-in iff some candidate strategy under the same 20-call/20-candidate budget has solveRate >= budgetMatchedStandard.solveRate + 0.10 AND has no premature early-stop, no budget violation, no empty solution, and a usable finalScore; otherwise do-not-add

baselineNote: standard_sampling natively uses 1 generate call. To honor the same-budget requirement, the decision baseline is standard_sampling repeated up to 20 times per task (same 20-call/20-candidate cap) with first-correct selection. The native 1-call result is reported separately; comparing a 20-call strategy to it would be a budget artifact.

completionProbe.consequence: with taskType=general the MCTS root (the problem text) is already complete, so mctsSearch takes the terminal branch, returns an empty solution, and reports 0 generateCalls; isCompleteMath is also case-sensitive, so a capitalized "The answer is" is not recognized as a math completion

limitations: synthetic candidates are independent and iid; real LLM candidates are correlated and the scoreFn would be noisy
the scoreFn is a perfect verifier (it knows the correct option), which favors best_of_n and the budget-matched standard baseline
the budget-matched standard baseline uses the same first-correct verifier as best_of_n to isolate search value; a majority-vote baseline would instead measure the value of having a verifier at all
MCTS uses Math.random for UCT tie-breaking and rollout selection, so its trajectory is not seed-reproducible
MCTS terminal simulation returns a completion-pattern reward without consulting scoreFn, so finalScore is not a correctness signal

taskType completion detection is a string heuristic; the synthetic "the answer is option X" format deliberately triggers the math pattern for the mcts_math control, while the capitalization probe shows that "The answer is ..." is not recognized
20 tasks per arm is a small sample; the difference between 0.2 and 0.2 can be noise, while the budget-matched baseline is near ceiling
actual generate calls are wrapper invocations, not token counts; a call with n candidates is one invocation here
